text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on January 3 in history.
1322 - Philip V of France died and was succeeded by his brother, Charles IV.
1698 - Italian poet Pietro Metastasio born; he was also famed for his "melodrammi" including "Ezio" and "La Clemenza di Tito" which were eventually set to music
1777 - In the American War of Independence, George Washington defeated the British under Lord Cornwallis at the Battle of Princeton.
1840 - Father Damien (Joseph de Veuster), Belgian priest and missionary, born; he was renowned for his work among the lepers of Molokai, a Hawaiian island.
1874 - Marshal Francisco Serrano became dictator of Spain.
1875 - French lexicographer Pierre Larousse, whose works included the "Grand Dictionnaire Universel du XIX Siecle", died.
1892 - J.R.R. Tolkien, British author of the "The Hobbit" and "The Lord of the Rings", born.
1907 - Ray Milland, U.S. film actor, born in Neath, Wales as Reginald Truscott-Jones; He won an Oscar in 1945 for the film "The Lost Weekend".
1909 - Danish pianist and entertainer Victor Borge born.
1924 - Howard Carter, British egyptologist, found the sarcophagus of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings near Luxor.
1926 - Theodoros Pangalos proclaimed himself dictator of Greece following a coup the previous June. He was deposed in August 1926.
1926 - Jaroslav Hasek, Czech writer and poet died famous for his masterly satire "The Good Soldier Schweik", died.
1946 - William Joyce, the "Lord Haw Haw" who broadcasted Nazi propaganda to Britain during World War Two, was hanged for treason in London.
1959 - Alaska became the 49th state to be admitted to the United States.
1961 - U.S. President Dwight Eisenhower broke off diplomatic relations with Cuba.
1967 - Jack Ruby, who shot Lee Harvey Oswald before he could be tried for the assassination of President Kennedy, died in hospital.
1980 - Joy Adamson, Austrian-born British naturalist and writer famous for the book "Born Free", was found murdered in Kenya.
1990 - 307 people were killed in southern Pakistan when an express train crashed into a freight train in the country's worst train disaster to date.
1993 - Presidents Boris Yeltsin and George Bush signed the Start-II Treaty, eliminating about two-thirds of the Russian and U.S. nuclear stockpiles.
1994 - All 124 people on board a Russian Tupolev-154 craft, operated by Baikal Air, were killed when it crashed near Mamony in Siberia.
